images.title: Five tiles and their outer edges
images.purpose: Show an L of 5 tiles with every one of its 12 outer edges marked 1, so that the perimeter is seen as the number of outer edges and the edges that tiles share are seen to be inside.
images.composition: The L of tiles on the left with each outer edge marked 1, two lines of working on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 62, the heading Five tiles in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). Left, a figure of exactly 5 square tiles shaped like the letter L, every tile 100 by 100 px filled amber #E69F00 with a thin dark #2B2B2B outline (3 px): 3 tiles in the top row at x 250 to 550 and y 150 to 250, and 2 more tiles in a column below the left tile at x 250 to 350 and y 250 to 450. Every outer edge of the figure carries the number 1 in dark #1F2937 sans-serif (30 px), placed 28 px outside the middle of the edge: there are exactly 12 such labels, at the points (300, 122), (400, 122), (500, 122), (578, 200), (400, 278), (500, 278), (378, 300), (378, 400), (300, 478), (222, 200), (222, 300), (222, 400). No label sits on an edge that two tiles share. To the right, at x 800, two lines of text: 12 outer edges at y 250 and Perimeter 12 at y 330 (44 px, dark #1F2937). In all 5 tiles, 12 outer edges, 12 labels 1 and 2 lines of text. No other number and no other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a figure with a number of tiles other than 5 or of outer edges marked other than 12
a label 1 on an edge shared by two tiles
images.takeaway: The perimeter of a figure of tiles is the number of its outer edges; the edges where tiles touch are inside.
images.description: Five square tiles placed like the letter L with its 12 outer edges each marked 1.
images.context: Concept image for Counting the Outer Edges of Tiles. It follows the idea of the tile figures in your maths book (every outer edge marked 1) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student tap each outer edge once as they count to 12. The slip to watch: counting an edge between two tiles.

image_decisions.why: The labelled outer edges make the perimeter of tiles countable at a glance.
